## ES-001 — P1: A post-commit code read can return failure after EVM state is committed

Anchor: `crates/hl-evm/src/executor.rs:2124` commits the transaction state;2129 then calls fallible `committed_contract_diffs`. That helper at506..524 reads each written code key and can return a database error or absent-key error. The failure branch rolls back only archived precompile-record consumption and returns an execution error before gas/diff publication. It does not undo the committed database. `rocks_db.rs:343..347` makes the preceding write synchronous and records direct write errors correctly.

Call path: tracked EVM transaction execution → snapshot/extract diff → DB commit → committed code-key reads → execution error. The writable Rocks backend can therefore retain a transaction whose accepted diff/gas/archive consumption was not published; a retry/restart using that DB cannot assume the pre-transaction state. Fatal engine latching protects subsequent normal application, but does not restore the durable write.

Verification gap: inject a failure specifically into the post-commit code-key read after a successful synchronous write, then inspect nonce/account/code state, returned diff and restart behavior. This audit does not demonstrate an occurrence or claim the checkpoint-backed in-memory replay overlay has the same durability consequence.

## ES-002 — P2: Commit cursors publish before fallible leader-input synchronization finishes

Anchor: `crates/hl-node/src/committed_applier.rs:469` advances the shared execution-round atomic before `inputs.sync` at474. A sync error then returns `EngineApplyFailed` and halts the applier at476..478. `crates/hl-consensus/src/staking_inputs.rs:44..46` also advances history's execution round before fallible profile/delegation/address projection at59..78; new stake/jail samples are installed only at80..82.

Call path: authenticated committed block → Exchange/hash guard succeeds → shared cursor advances → leader history round advances → sample projection fails → error/halt. The error leaves both progress cursors advanced without completing the corresponding leader-input update. The halt prevents later applier mutation; consumers of the shared cursor/history are nevertheless not given an all-or-nothing publication boundary. Concurrent observation during successful synchronization is an additional hypothesis, not established by a scheduling test here.

Verification gap: force a typed staking-projection error and assert cursor/history/sample consistency and how the runtime advertises or resumes that round. Inspect reader synchronization before claiming a live authentication consequence.

## ES-003 — P2: Explicit EVM inputs are paired with each other, not with the loaded L1 checkpoint

Anchors: `crates/hl-node/src/replay.rs:1614..1641`,2417..2449; `evm_checkpoint.rs:20..59`. The normal explicit path verifies matching numeric EVM directory heights and canonical roots for the DB and sidecar. It never compares that EVM height to the loaded L1 snapshot context. The shared loader trusts the supplied sidecar and validates readable accounts/code; it neither recomputes all three accumulator categories nor checks storage records there.

Call path: load L1 RMP → choose explicit DB/sidecar → compare those two paths → load accumulators → attach executor. An otherwise readable DB/sidecar pair from height H2 can pass these guards while the L1 snapshot is H1. Co-location also does not establish sidecar/content equality. This admits a synthetic prestate through configuration; it does not establish that the retained Native pairs used by the current gates were mismatched.

Verification gap: a negative startup control with distinct L1/EVM heights, and a co-located altered Es/sidecar case, should fail before forward execution. Retain existing source manifests and Native pair certificates; directory equality alone is a weaker proof.

## ES-004 — P2: Explicit forward checkpoint loading does not enforce the completion marker

Anchors: `crates/hl-evm/src/checkpoint_import.rs:76..82`,94..106; `official_checkpoint_db.rs:84..91`; `executor.rs:995..1001`. Imported batches disable WAL before `finish` flushes and writes sidecar plus completion marker. The forward executor factory opens the official database through an adapter that checks neither sidecar nor marker. The shared validation loader likewise has no marker guard. Main's automatic latest-checkpoint discovery uses the marker, but explicit forward paths bypass that discovery.

Call path: interrupted import or explicit incomplete directory → official DB open succeeds if RocksDB is readable → executor attaches. This contradicts the importer's stated invariant that a crash before the marker leaves nothing loadable. An incomplete DB with an available supplied sidecar can reach explicit initialization; marker absence is not rejected by these APIs. The importer itself legitimately opens the pre-marker DB to rebuild hashes, so raw inspection and forward-admission APIs need distinct readiness contracts.

Verification gap: interrupted import at each flush/sidecar/marker boundary, followed by explicit startup, plus power-loss durability checks for sidecar/marker writes. No crash test was run.

## ES-005 — P2: `live-follow` can degrade requested full EVM execution to no executor

Anchors: `crates/hl-node/src/live_follow.rs:153..170`,195..215,352..386; `exchange.rs:12477..12496`. When a requested EVM path fails to open, this public CLI path logs a warning and continues. It calls the writable a/c/s Rocks adapter rather than the official E* checkpoint adapter; an official-layout path is therefore not the same prestate route as current replay. Sidecar loading does not bind its root to that executor path. The engine documents that EVM cadence is a no-op without an attached executor, while live-follow continues computing/reporting response-window matches.

Call path: LiveFollow CLI → requested DB initialization → failure/warning → continued L1 processing → response hash statistics. The mode can omit requested EVM execution while still producing response-match counts. The warning is visible; the behavior is not silent in logs. Response hashes alone do not certify EVM state. Current `CommittedBlockApplier::new_live` separately requires an attached executor and is not this degraded path.

Verification gap: a requested unreadable DB must cause startup failure in this CLI; an official-layout checkpoint should use the official adapter with pair validation. A runtime control should distinguish response matches from full EVM checkpoint identity. No affected active service was inspected or changed.

## ES-006 — P2: Replay's start-height filter compares consensus rounds

Anchors: `crates/hl-node/src/replay.rs:202..203`,1836..1845,2389..2390. `ReplayConfig.start_height` is documented as the first block height, but `raw_block_height` returns the inner `round`. The warmup/selected-prefix branch compares that round to `start_height`. Height and consensus round differ in current mainnet inputs.

Call path: configured first L1 height → input selector reads consensus round → warmup decision uses unlike units → selected response/checkpoint window differs from the requested height. For example, a height-valued start inside the H1175840000 window is below that window's R147867xxxx rounds, so it does not select the intended in-window height boundary. The same helper correctly compares round against `loaded_round`; that is a separate use which must remain in the round domain.

Verification gap: an input fixture carrying distinct L1 height/round values should prove selected block identity and warmup count. No replay was launched. Root's already-fixed runner failure propagation is excluded from these findings.

## Retained safeguards and scope

Primary tracked Rocks commits use synchronous WriteBatch and propagate their recorded write error. Execution/hashing guards latch fatal errors before subsequent application. Current replay's official adapter, chain ID from the loaded snapshot, and DB/sidecar canonical-root checks provide useful normal-path safeguards. Native mainnet checkpoint/accumulator evidence remains separate from these untested failure paths.

Full crash/restart certification still needs a joint L1 snapshot/EVM state/cursor recovery contract and targeted storage-fault controls. `save_full_snapshot` and diagnostic dumps write directly without an atomic rename/fsync protocol, but their production recovery role was not closed in this bounded pass, so no seventh finding is asserted. The generic stage pipeline and remaining storage backends were read only for context; no full-pipeline acceptance claim follows.

evidence.text:
# Replay and checkpoint certification system audit

Read-only authority: `[retained host artifact]`, plus the owned input/controller artifacts under `[retained host artifact]` and `[retained host artifact]`. No Source/script edit, build, test replay, Native execution, service operation or archival-tree write occurred. Findings below concern certification machinery, not new engine parity conclusions. Three pure-data counterexamples are saved in `static-counterexamples.json`.

The current reference attempt is **not certified**, and its existing artifacts say so. At inspection it has 454 checkpoint report files, an exact contiguous 45-checkpoint prefix through H1175795000, seven gap journal rows, no terminal `report/summary.json`, no `exit.json`, no final-state journal row, and a partial final JSON line. The retained successful/failed journal rows span 455429 records through H1176205429; 41401 carry parsed native expected-response hashes, of which 10520 match. These are stopped-prefix observations, not 500k acceptance. The input manifest separately certifies 50 source windows/500000 records/45455 native footer keys; input completeness does not certify their execution. `root-stop-20261009.json` explicitly records persistent divergence and `execution_certified:false`.

Six concrete defects or verification gaps follow. Existing manual false-certification safeguards are acknowledged separately; none of these findings asserts that this failed reference run was reported as a PASS.

## 1. P1 — replay process success is not a parity verdict

**Call path:** `crates/hl-node/src/main.rs:1312..1317` calls `run_replay_audited` and counts response matches; `main.rs:1543..1552` returns an error only for failed explicitly supplied app-hash truth or `read_archive_failure`. It does not fail on `mismatch_count`. `replay.rs:2044..2046` merely breaks on `--stop-on-mismatch`, then `replay.rs:2226` returns `Ok(ReplayRun)`.

State-tree comparisons are weaker still: `ReplayRunner::check_abci_tree`, `replay.rs:823..853`, prints/writes `TreeReport` but returns the computed optional hash regardless of `digest MATCH/MISMATCH`. Native exchange-tree comparison failures are not aggregated into the CLI summary's `app_hash_mismatched` counter; that counter belongs to the distinct explicit app-hash-expected facility (`main.rs:1364..1375`).

`replay.rs:1767..1769` returns an empty successful run when no files are found. `replay.rs:1821..1825` warns and skips a file whose initial input stream cannot be opened. Reaching terminal code therefore does not imply requested count, native response equality, checkpoint equality or even nonempty replay.

**Impact:** a controller that treats exit status zero, “Replay complete”, or response-only summary as certification can falsely accept mismatches or incomplete execution. The owned prerequisite gate checker additionally inspects results and tree files, so it does not rely on exit status alone; its remaining holes are finding 3. The reference controller deliberately writes `execution_certified:false`.

**Finite correction/proof:** expose a structured terminal verification verdict with response mismatches, state-tree failures, expected/observed counts, input-open failures and completion status. Preserve a diagnostic mode if zero exit on known mismatch is intentional; certification must explicitly require the strict verdict. Verify mismatch, stop-on-mismatch, empty input and unreadable bucket cases without Native execution.

## 2. P1 — checkpoint oracle coverage and duplicate conflicts are not certified

**Call path:** `replay.rs:1774..1779` loads available Native exchange-tree lines into a map. `replay.rs:813..815` silently returns `Ok(None)` for a replayed height absent from that map. No expected checkpoint-height schedule or “missing truth” count is emitted, and there is no final assertion that every required checkpoint was compared.

`crates/hl-engine/src/abci_tree/mod.rs:490..517` selects the earliest timestamp at each height. Multiple versions are not recorded in the report. Equal-timestamp conflicts retain the first traversal encounter (`:512..514`), while directory iteration order at `:500..502` is unspecified. This intentionally collapses restart copies but does not certify that duplicate selected truth is identical or belongs to the frozen checkpoint provenance.

The fast height prefilter at `abci_tree/mod.rs:522..526` searches literal `"height":` and reads digits immediately after the colon. Valid JSON `{"height": 123,...}` yields no height and is silently skipped before actual tree parsing. The compact and spaced examples in `static-counterexamples.json` have the same JSON height but different prefilter results.

**Impact:** missing/format-skipped/conflicting truth can reduce the number of state comparisons without a fatal replay result. A smaller complete-looking report set is not “all Native checkpoints”. This does not claim the current Native compact writer emitted whitespace or conflicting copies; these are concrete unchecked input paths.

**Finite correction/proof:** freeze an expected height set and Native oracle file/content manifest before replay; require exact equality with observed comparison heights, reject inconsistent duplicates and report the selected truth provenance. Parse the height through JSON or accept JSON whitespace in the prefilter. Check missing, duplicate-identical, duplicate-conflicting and whitespace cases with local data fixtures.

## 3. P1 — prerequisite gate acceptance checks file count and a substring, not exact checkpoint results

**Owned code:** `latest-mainnet-continuous-500k-reference/run_after_gates.py:46..49` requires `len(abci_tree_*.txt)==checkpoints`, then `re.search` for one matching `SUMMARY <any digits> ... 60/60 ... digest MATCH` inside each file.

It does not verify the expected checkpoint-height set, the filename/embedded-height agreement, exactly one SUMMARY per file, or absence of a MISMATCH summary. A file containing a matching SUMMARY followed by a mismatching SUMMARY satisfies its expression; the pure-data reproduction is saved. Ten unrelated or stale matching-height reports satisfy the count check as well. The checker does validate requested block/response counts, Native-supplied-only response scope, gap-zero log marker and retained final SHA (`:37..55`); those are useful independent protections but do not repair the checkpoint-set/content hole.

**Impact:** stale/mixed artifacts can promote a prerequisite independent window as passing even though its exact required state-checkpoint set was not proved. Current retained artifacts do contain terminal gate results; this finding describes the predicate's insufficiency, not an observed gate substitution.

**Finite correction/proof:** accept only a fresh run directory with a manifest; compare exact expected/report height sets, parse one final structured checkpoint result per height, require all 60 fields/digest exact and reject any duplicate/conflicting result. Bind these results to the command/input/run identity. An isolated fake report directory can verify the predicate; do not run Native or another replay.

## 4. P2 — input, rules, Native truth, source and prerequisite binary binding are incomplete

**Owned code:** `run_after_gates.py:71..72` verifies the chosen frozen executable against its own `executable-sha256.txt`. `:73..75` trusts cached input status; `:77` copies the old input manifest. It does not rehash actual `SOURCE/inputs` consumed by the command, verify prerequisite gates used that same executable, or bind the gate's Source/rules/bootstrap/Native oracle/EVM inputs into `gates.json`/`started.json`.

Source collectors `latest-mainnet-continuous-500k-source/audit.py:17..27` and `audit-complete500k.py:6..25` correctly check stable source stats/content, sequential source heights and increasing rounds, and stage hardlinks. However the controller later consumes those mutable directory entries using only cached status. The completed-input provenance is separate from runtime consumption provenance. The copied L1 snapshot and Native `--abci-hashes` path (`run_after_gates.py:95/99`) are not content-bound in the start record; copied runtime rules `:91..92` are not hashed there either.

**Impact:** the frozen executable's SHA is proved, but that alone does not prove “this Source candidate passed these gates against these exact inputs”. Later directory/source/rules/Native-oracle replacement or an older gate artifact can be associated with a newer invocation. No such replacement is alleged for the current stopped run; the missing machine-checkable join is the verification gap.

**Finite correction/proof:** record and check one immutable run manifest joining executable SHA, compiled feature/rules identity, execution-Source hashes, command, exact replica file hashes, L1 bootstrap hash, EVM bootstrap identity, Native checkpoint oracle hashes and each prerequisite gate's same executable identity. Recheck staged consumption files at launch or stage verified immutable copies. Compare final manifest identity before any certificate publication.

## 5. P2 — gap census loses simultaneous unsupported reasons and can only describe a contaminated prefix

**Call path:** `exchange.rs:6981..6984` takes and clears both the Exchange unsupported latch and clearinghouse reservation latch, then returns `own.or(reservation)`. If both are set with distinct reasons, the second reason is erased without a census row. `exchange.rs:7000..7003` also retains only the first Exchange poison reason. `gap_census.rs:record` records that single normalized string as one block/arm.

`replay.rs:1927..1934` records a gap, increments attempted block count and continues to the next input without rollback or completing that block. The module documentation correctly states subsequent state is no longer Native. `BlockLog::gap` omits committed height and any expected Native footer; the CLI `summary.json` has no census arm/count field. A interrupted census run therefore cannot rely on a terminal GAP_CENSUS marker or a response-summary denominator to count all attempted/gapped inputs. The current stopped journal has seven explicit gap rows and no terminal summary.

**Impact:** “every unmodelled arm” overstates the census inventory. Clearing two latches but emitting one can hide an independent unsupported path; post-gap comparisons are diagnostic, not acceptance. A zero-gap terminal run remains useful—this finding does not turn a genuine zero count into nonzero.

**Finite correction/proof:** preserve each taken reason independently and carry committed height, input identity, expected-footer presence and contaminated-state status in gap rows/summary. Keep certification fail-closed at the first gap; use continuing census only as a backlog tool. Validate two simultaneous latches and a truncated census journal with local fixtures.

## 6. P1 verification gap — there is no terminal continuous-500k acceptance auditor in the owned controller

**Owned code:** `run_after_gates.py:93..109` constructs and starts one replay command. It creates a fresh writable EVM bootstrap (`:78..90`, refusing an existing checkpoint), so this attempt's construction genuinely supports a single runtime; it does not stitch the three prerequisite windows. But `:122..124` only records exit status with `execution_certified:false` and says an independent acceptance audit is required. No terminal validator is provided in the inspected owned directories to check the full one-bootstrap acceptance conditions.

`bootstrap_count:1` and `continuous_runtime:true` in the start record (`:103..105`) are declarations, not a journal-to-process/command/content binding. `BlockLog::create` opens/truncates its file and per-block rows have no run ID or executable/parent-state link; checkpoint reports overwrite by height (`replay.rs:826..837`). Fresh-EVM refusal protects this particular normal controller path, but a future separately resumed/reused report directory must not be certified just from these report filenames and declarations.

Response truth is sparse: `replay.rs:904..908` compares only string-valued Native `resps.Hash`; `main.rs:1353` correctly names this `native-supplied-only`. Source input auditors count any `Hash` key (`audit.py:21`, `audit-complete500k.py:20`), whereas replay silently treats a non-string value as absent. The saved example `Hash:17` is counted by the collector but supplies no replay expectation. A terminal certificate must reconcile per-input valid footer identity/denominator, not assert all 500000 response bytes were Native checked. The current complete-source manifest has 45455 footer keys, separate from 500000 records.

**Finite correction/proof:** add a separate artifact-only acceptance validator requiring one bound bootstrap/process/run lineage, exactly 500000 consecutive committed heights through the target endpoint, no gaps, terminal completion/final-state row, every required Native checkpoint exactly once with all 60 fields/digest MATCH, all valid Native-supplied response hashes compared/matched, full EVM execution and the joined input/source/executable manifest. Explicitly reject prefix-only, independently rebootstraped, mixed/restarted, truncated and malformed-footer artifacts. Three separate perfect 10k prerequisite windows are useful regressions; they cannot stand in for this continuous certificate.

## Relation to the root operational audit

Root separately identified and is fixing `tools/run_window.sh` exit-code masking, same-tag evidence deletion and global-fixture snapshot precedence. Those are distinct wrapper defects; this packet does not duplicate their implementation. Current acceptance commands are private frozen command controllers rather than that generic script. Fixing the wrapper alone does not close the six certification concerns above.

## Existing protections retained

The owned input auditors do check exact record counts/height continuity and source SHA/stability when collection runs. The controller does check its selected executable SHA, prerequisite response counts, gap-zero marker, retained final-state SHA, fresh writable EVM bootstrap and disk margin. It never writes a successful execution certificate itself. Main CLI does fail explicit app-hash truth and archived read failures. These protections explain why the currently stopped reference run remains explicitly uncertified despite the automation hazards found here.

Source/owned-script hashes, exact source HEAD/status, inspected file excerpts and observed artifact statistics are retained in this packet. No current complete-500k or live-node certificate is claimed.
